fichas.title: Traffic calming measures and effects
fichas.summary: Overview of traffic-calming measures for residential roads, organized by traffic system (A), detailed layout (B), and traffic control (C). The table indicates desired, probable, and possible effects, including speed reduction, pedestrian safety, noise reduction, and changes to residential character.
figure_refs: 1 Traffic calming of roads in residential areas: overview of measures and effects
cross_refs: A1 blind alleys / culs de sac
B1 change of road surface material
B3 visual rearrangement of road space
C3 change of priority for drivers

fichas.title: Spatial layout of traffic management priorities
fichas.summary: Schematic diagram differentiating areas for pedestrians and cyclists, areas where slow traffic has priority or priority is shared, and areas where motor traffic has priority. The plan shows central and residential areas, local destinations, and connections to town and regional main roads.
spaces: Grass and trees play and sports area
figure_refs: 2 Schematic diagram of the spatial layout of traffic management priorities

fichas.title: Road layout proposal A
fichas.summary: Proposal for separating driving and pedestrian areas, reducing road width in favour of wider pavements, and slowing traffic through narrowing and partial use of raised paving. The accompanying text describes increased pedestrian space and safety through spatial subdivision.
cross_refs: B1 + B2 + B3 + (where appropriate, B4 + B6) + C1 + C2

fichas.title: Road layout proposal B
fichas.summary: A fully reorganized shared street layout combines driving, parking, and walking in a common mixed area to enable multiple uses of the whole road space. The layout prioritizes residential needs and limits vehicles to walking pace or the stated maximum speed.
uses: Shared use of the road space

dimensions.label: Maximum speed
dimensions.context: Vehicle speed in the shared-area layout; the text also specifies walking pace
